```{r}
#| label: load_packages
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# List of packages used in analysis
packagelist <- c("tidyverse", "here", "devtools", "knitr", "patchwork", "kableExtra", "lubridate", "glue", "cowplot", "brms", "tidybayes", "ggforce", "ggstance", "parallel", "rstan", "ellipse") 

# Install packages if not already installed
invisible(lapply(packagelist, function(package){if ( !package %in% rownames(installed.packages())) {install.packages(package)}} ))

# Load required CRAN packages
invisible(lapply(packagelist, library, character.only = T, quietly = T))

# Load papaja
library(papaja) # if not installed: devtools::install_github("crsh/papaja")

theme_set(theme_cowplot())

# Use several cores in parallel
ncores = detectCores()
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)  # to avoid recompilation of unchanged Stan programs
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores()) # for execution on a local, multicore CPU with excess RAM
```

```{r}
my_citations_full <- cite_r(file = "04_chapters/r-references.bib", footnote = FALSE)
```

## R packages used
As indicated in the Methods section, for all our analyses we used `r my_citations_full`.

## Supplementary Figures
<!-- average results on probability scale for the first and second lattice -->
```{r}
#| child: "04_chapters/fig-avgdata-prop.Rmd"
#| eval: false
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-avgprop
#| fig-cap: "<small>(a) Mean response to the first stimulus dependent on aspect ratio (percentage). The probability of responding 0&deg; to the first stimulus decreases with aspect ratio (|a|/|b|). The value of aspect ratio increases with increasing distance in the 0&deg;-orientation, leading to more 90&deg; responses. (b) Mean response to the second stimulus dependent on aspect ratio (percentage). The probability of responding 0&deg; to the second stimulus increases with aspect ratio (|a|/|b|; i.e., adaptation effect), and increases when the first stimulus was perceived as 0&deg; rather than 90&deg; (i.e., hysteresis effect). Dots indicate observed values. In addition, mean posterior predictions and their 95% highest density continuous intervals are shown.</small>"
if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
include_graphics(here("04_figs", "avgprop.pdf"))
}
if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
include_graphics(here("04_figs", "avgprop.svg"))
}
```

<!-- individual results on probability scale for the first and second lattice -->
```{r}
#| child: "04_chapters/fig-indivdata-prop.Rmd"

```

```{r}
#| label: fig-indivprop
#| fig-cap: "<small>(a) Mean individual responses to the first stimulus dependent on aspect ratio (percentage). The probability of responding 0&deg; to the first stimulus decreases with aspect ratio (|a|/|b|). The value of aspect ratio increases with increasing distance in the 0&deg;-orientation, leading to more 90&deg; responses. Dots indicate observed values. In addition, mean posterior predictions and their 95% highest density continuous intervals are shown. Plots for participants with the smallest and largest estimated proximity effect are indicated in red. (b) Mean individual responses to the second stimulus dependent on aspect ratio (percentage). The probability of responding 0&deg; to the second stimulus increases with aspect ratio (|a|/|b|; i.e., adaptation effect), and increases when the first stimulus was perceived as 0&deg; rather than 90&deg; (i.e., hysteresis effect). Dots indicate observed values. In addition, mean posterior predictions and their 95% highest density continuous intervals are shown. Plots for participants with the smallest and largest estimated hysteresis effect are indicated in blue, participants with the smallest and largest estimated adaptation effect are indicated in red.</small>"

if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
include_graphics(here("04_figs", "indivprop.pdf"))
}
if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
include_graphics(here("04_figs", "indivprop.svg"))
}
```

The probability of responding 0&deg; to the second stimulus increases with aspect ratio (|a|/|b|; i.e., adaptation effect), and increases when the first stimulus was perceived as 0&deg; rather than 90&deg; (i.e., hysteresis effect). Dots indicate observed values. In addition, mean posterior predictions and their 95% highest density continuous intervals are shown.</small>"
```{r}
#|

```
